findings.description: `reset_bucket(provider, auth_type=...)` treats an explicitly named bucket as a match even when no state file exists. With `auth_type` provided it sets `targets = [auth_type]`, reads the default state, writes a new CLOSED state file, appends the bucket to `done`, and returns success.
findings.failure_mode: `cheval --reset-breaker google:http_api` or `python -m loa_cheval.routing.breaker_cli --reset google:http_api` will create a new breaker bucket and exit 0 even when nothing matched, violating the documented contract that the command exits 1 when nothing matched. This can also pollute `.run` with fabricated healthy breaker state for buckets that never existed.
findings.suggested_fix: When `auth_type` is provided, verify the bucket exists in `list_buckets(run_dir).get(provider, {})` or by validating the expected state file before journaling/writing. Return `[]` without writing when it does not exist; keep the current behavior for existing CLOSED buckets.
